title: Castagna Milano’s One-Off Roadster Started Life as an Alfa Giulia Quadrifoglio
summary: Alfa Romeo hasn’t sold a mass-market convertible since the Brera-based Spider retired in 2011, and it left the drop-top segment entirely when it ended production of the 4C Spider in 2020. It doesn’t sound like the brand will launch another convertible soon, so Italian coachbuilder Castagna Milano has turned the Giulia into a one-off roadster […]
body_markdown:
Alfa Romeo hasn’t sold a mass-market convertible since the Brera-based Spider retired in 2011, and it left the drop-top segment entirely when it ended production of[the 4C Spider](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/alfa-romeo-to-celebrate-its-mid-engine-heritage-with-limited-edition-4c-spider-33-stradale-tributo/) in 2020. It doesn’t sound like the brand will launch another convertible soon, so Italian coachbuilder Castagna Milano has turned[the Giulia](https://www.hagerty.com/media/new-car-reviews/2024-alfa-romeo-giulia-competizione-review-a-plenty-sweet-pot-as-is/) into a one-off roadster that looks nothing like the sedan it’s based on.


The exterior styling falls in the “love it or hate it” category. The front end features thin LED lights, Y-shaped trim that almost looks Lamborghini-esque, with plenty of exposed carbon fiber. Out back, Castagna Milano added lights integrated into a sharp character line that runs around the entire car, vents in the wheel arches, and four exhaust outlets positioned on either side of a wide diffuser.


It’s the proportions that really set Castagna Milano’s roadster apart from the Giulia, however. The dashboard, the steering wheel, and the front seats were moved back by nearly 13 inches. The shift delivers the typical GT look, with a long hood and a short trunk lid, without drastically changing the car’s dimensions. The model (which hasn’t been given a name yet) stretches about 185 inches long, 54 inches tall, and 76 inches wide. The Giulia measures 183 inches long, 56 inches tall, and 73 inches wide.


We haven’t seen pictures of the interior yet, but the coachbuilder notes that it developed the Giulia-based roadster as a two-seater with a 22-cubic-foot trunk (compared to around 13 cubes in the Giulia), thinner A-pillars for better visibility, and a folding soft top with a rear window that doubles as a wind deflector. The cabin offers two types of leather upholstery as well as fossil wood trim.

The roadster is based on[the Giulia Quadrifoglio](https://www.hagerty.com/media/new-car-reviews/track-review-2022-alfa-romeo-giulia-quadrifoglio-has-still-got-it/) , so it’s powered by a twin-turbocharged, 2.9-liter V-6. We’re curious to find out what it’s like to drive: Moving the cabin back shifts the weight distribution. Castagna Milano promises revised final-drive gearing, and the carbon-fiber body panels help lower weight to around 3130 pounds, down from about 3570 pounds for a European-spec Giulia Quadrifoglio. The front and rear tracks were widened to match the GTAm’s, which was[a limited-run track-focused variant](https://www.hagerty.com/media/motorsports/alfa-romeo-launches-track-focused-540-hp-giulia-gta-and-gtam/) .


If you like Castagna Milano’s take on the Giulia, you’re in luck: They will build the car. It hasn’t been completed yet, so the buyer will be able to work directly with the coachbuilder to personalize the car, and we’re told that it can be homologated for road use and built relatively quickly. Pricing hasn’t been announced, and it likely depends on the cost of the donor car and the final specifications.


This isn’t the first time we’ve seen a coachbuilder give the Alfa Romeo Giulia a completely new look. Earlier in 2026, an Italian company named SGT Automobili unveiled[a limited-edition, Giulia-based restomod](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/sgt-automobili-55-sgt-giulia-restomod-pictures-specs/) called 55-SGT inspired by the 155 DTM that raced in the 1990s. The boxy four-door also uses the Quadrifoglio’s twin-turbo V-6. Given a Giulia to modify and a blank check, would you turn it into the futuristic-looking roadster or the heritage-laced sedan?
